name: ALGOL 68
note: orthogonal design; standardised parallel clauses with semaphores
typeSystem: Static, with a highly orthogonal design: essentially any type could be combined with any type constructor (arrays, structures, procedures, references, unions), a generality that strongly influenced later language design even though it made the language notoriously difficult to implement.
runtime: Implemented by several execution strategies: historical compilers generated native code, some systems translated ALGOL 68 to C, and ALGOL 68 Genie primarily interprets the language with optional dynamic compilation of eligible units.

runtimes.name: Native compilers (historical and GCC ga68)
runtimes.role: Historical implementations compiled to machine code; GCC 16 added the experimental ga68 front end.

runtimes.name: ALGOL 68 Genie
runtimes.role: Primarily interprets a syntax tree, with an optional unit compiler that emits, compiles, and dynamically links C for eligible units.

runtimes.name: Source-to-C implementations
runtimes.role: Implementations such as Algol68toC translate ALGOL 68 to C for portability.

concurrencyModel: The standard included 'parallel clauses' (par begin...end) with semaphores for synchronisation - one of the earliest mainstream languages to standardise concurrency directly.
